parts:
For the table question, you can pass the renderTable function the arguments include.rownames=FALSE and include.colnames=FALSE. However, I just tried it and include.colnames doesn't seem to have any effect, unfortunately; it appears to be a bug in the xtable library. You could add some CSS (see this article) to do a rule like:

#id_of_your_table th {
  display: none;
}

As for your original question, there isn't a direct way to get the labels from the UI. But keep in mind the UI can be generated programmatically, so you could have a single "source of truth" that describes the choices defined in global.R, and then build the UI off of that in ui.R.

For example:

global.R
=======
x_choices <- c(
  "Foo" = "foo",
  "Bar" = "bar",
  "Baz" = "baz"
)

ui.R
====
shinyUI(selectInput("x", "X", x_choices))

server.R
====
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$x)) {
      message("The choices were: ", paste(names(x_choices), collapse = ","), " and the user chose ", input$x)
    }
  })
})
